answer: Persistent Presence Ledger. Each identity must answer randomized micro-prompts within a narrow time window; missed prompts decay its reputation, a slow glacier of lost standing. An island of verified history unlocks transaction rights only after sustained, non-outsourceable response streaks. Because attention cannot be parallelized, each duplicate identity consumes real operator hours. An ember of reputation needs constant tending, so an attacker running N sybils pays N times the sustained attention cost, making mass duplication economically irrational.
